games.name: Tide and Retreat
games.definingDecision: Move along connected intersections and choose approach or withdrawal to capture the contiguous enemy line in front of or behind the mover; a capture chain cannot revisit an intersection or repeat its preceding direction.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No jump-over capture, promotion or diagonal checker lanes: one adjacent move can sweep a whole line on either side, and chain-direction/history constraints change continuations.

games.controls: Select a pawn, adjacent empty intersection, and approach/withdraw when both capture; Finish chain may end an optional continuation.
games.finite: Three opposed tactical positions with progressively longer capture opportunities.

endless.design: New seeded sparse balanced capture positions, fresh opponent tie ordering, campaign score until defeat; board size and search depth capped.

games.failure: Lose all pawns or mobility; repetition/turn limit resolves by material rather than an endless cycle.
games.levelsGeneration: Connected 5x5 intersection graph; authored first studies, seeded later tactical positions certified for legal starts.

games.name: Spore Council
games.definingDecision: Clone to an adjacent square or jump two squares leaving the source empty; every adjacent enemy around the landing becomes yours. Cloning grows material but may expose a conversion cluster.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Moves originate from existing pieces, with an irreversible clone-versus-jump choice; conversion touches all eight neighbors and never requires bracketed rays.

games.controls: Select your colony, then a highlighted one- or two-step landing.
games.finite: Three 5x5 boards with increasingly obstructed geometry and tactical opponent.

endless.design: Seeded symmetric rock patterns and varied openings; same bounded board, opponent depth capped, cumulative survival score.

games.failure: Elimination or lower material at saturation; pass only when no landing exists, repeated boards terminate by material.
games.levelsGeneration: Start from opposed corners with a connected legal empty region; inspect generated moves and rock symmetry.

games.name: Shared Comet
games.definingDecision: First slide the shared neutral comet as far as possible along a clear ray, then slide one of your blockers; plan where the opponent will be forced to send that same comet.

nearestExisting.differentiator: A shared compulsory neutral piece determines immediate home-edge victories; blockers move without permanently closing squares or shooting arrows.

games.controls: Tap a comet endpoint, then select a friendly blocker and a ray endpoint.
games.finite: Three opposed neutral-token races with distinct blocker formations.

endless.design: Seeded legal blocker arrangements on a fixed 5x5 board, changing comet starts, stage score until opponent wins.

games.failure: Comet reaches opposing home edge, or a player cannot complete the required comet/blocker turn; repetition resolves visibly.
games.levelsGeneration: Authored teaching formations plus seeded legal positions; generated starts exclude already won edges.

games.name: Socket Skirmish
games.definingDecision: Spend a turn fitting a directional movement pod to a piece or execute a straight jump using one of its installed directions; jumped opposing pieces and their pods become captured reserves.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Movement permissions are persistent player-built directions attached to individual pieces, purchased using finite pods; no exchanged communal movement cards.
Capture recycles movement hardware, while opponent pieces remain captured and cannot be redeployed as units.

games.controls: Choose piece, then Install direction or a highlighted movement/capture endpoint.
games.finite: Three small opposed positions requiring different installed movement networks.

endless.design: Seeded starting pod configurations, objective-home locations and reserve budgets on fixed board; opponent planning cap disclosed.

games.failure: Lose your home square or all pieces; installing a pod spends the turn and can concede a tactical attack.
games.levelsGeneration: 5x5 board, finite pieces/pods, deterministic heuristic opponent, varied legal reserve and socket configurations.

games.name: Cannon Council
games.definingDecision: Three aligned soldiers form a cannon. Reposition the formation by shifting its rear soldier to the front, or bombard beyond an empty muzzle gap; ordinary soldiers fight at short range.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Attack range and legal translation arise from an emergent aligned three-piece formation, with no action-point pool, directional cover, suppression, or overwatch.

games.controls: Select a soldier, then move/capture, shift-cannon or bombard buttons.
games.finite: Three battle positions with defended towns and increasing competing formations.

endless.design: Seeded town placement, soldier patterns and obstacle-free bounded fields; increasingly capable but capped opponent.

games.failure: Your town is destroyed or no soldiers remain; opponent town destruction wins immediately.
games.levelsGeneration: Compact 5x5 formation geometry with explicit ranged ray checks and fixed maximum game length.

games.name: Bloom Cauldron
games.definingDecision: Build a persistent bag of ingredients, then draw without replacement into a growing pot; colored ingredients multiply earlier colors, while too many white hazards spoil the batch. Stop drawing before buying improvements.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No hand/action/treasure deck loop: a pot accumulates spatial position and interactions as a bag is exhausted; stopping trades expected gain against a hazard threshold, and purchases alter future draw probabilities.
Player changes the probability distribution permanently and resolves color-combination effects; no memoryless single-die repeated wager.

games.controls: Draw ingredient, Bottle batch, then buy a labeled ingredient or clean one hazard.
games.finite: Three independently seeded three-market brewing studies, with score and solvent batch quotas.

endless.design: New seeded brewing seasons with changing public recipes, deterministic bag order seeded per season, cumulative score until bankruptcy.

games.failure: Spills consume batch income and finite reserve; missing recipe/solvency target loses the study.
games.levelsGeneration: Bounded ingredient counts and hazard threshold; shuffled bags preserve visible composition and use no hidden test answer.

games.name: Three Fronts
games.definingDecision: Allocate one finite force simultaneously across three independently valued battlefields; concentration wins locally but concedes others, and rival allocations adapt to your revealed previous pattern.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Each decision partitions a total budget across simultaneous multiple contests; there is no one-use ranked card for one sequential prize.
Opponent optimizes competing deployment under the same force conservation, without voyage schedules, escorts, cargo packing or permanent casualties.

games.controls: Increment/decrement three allocations, then Lock deployment.
games.finite: Three five-round matches with unequal battlefield values, ties and opponent behavioral classes.

endless.design: Seeded field values and opponent response parameters produce new bounded matches until a match loss.

games.failure: Lower total battlefield points after the match loses; empty fields are still valid strategic concessions.
games.levelsGeneration: Budget 8-12, three fields, explicit tie rule, rival forecast history instead of hidden future orders.

games.name: Package Yard
games.definingDecision: Submit mutually exclusive bids for complementary bundles of lots; the clearing auction selects a disjoint collection of bids maximizing revenue, so winning one desired lot can block a higher-value package.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Overlapping multi-lot packages, complementarity, and exclusive bid sets require combinatorial market clearing; individual high-card comparison cannot resolve allocations.
Prices and allocations emerge competitively from a bid book instead of buying at fixed posted item prices.

games.controls: Select package, adjust bid, include/exclude it, then Clear auction.
games.finite: Three auctions with six lots, published house bid books, and different complementary fulfillment contracts.

endless.design: Seeded values, nonoverlapping target recipes and overlapping competing package books; bounded six-lot exhaustive clearing.

games.failure: Overspend budget or fail target package utility; auction results list winning bundles, paid amount and unused lots.
games.levelsGeneration: Generated books include meaningful competing incompatible packages and a feasible budget-compatible target.

games.name: Falling Hammer
games.definingDecision: Wait as a Dutch auction clock lowers its price, or stop it now before a rival with a behavioral reservation policy takes the lot; preserve liquidity for later complementary objects.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Timing against a descending price clock, public valuation intervals and irreversible stop decisions replace simultaneous sealed rank bids.
The player chooses the purchase stopping time, an opponent can preempt, and object-specific complementary value replaces a public commodity calendar.

games.controls: Stop clock to buy or Wait one tick; rival acquisition and price change are resolved immediately.
games.finite: Three four-lot auctions with different complementary collections and reserve constraints.

endless.design: New seeded lot values, visible reservation ranges and complementary contracts on a bounded clock.

games.failure: Final collection value net of paid prices falls below quota, or spending denies an essential later object.
games.levelsGeneration: Rival reservation draws use seeded published distributions; every finite auction has source-verified attainable quota.

games.name: Orderbook Wharf
games.definingDecision: Post buy or sell limit orders at chosen prices, compete for time-priority fills, cancel scarce orders, and decide whether to cross the spread before future demand arrives.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No automatic execution at one public day's price: price-time priority and player-selected limit prices determine whether an order fills and how inventory exposure persists.
Orders trade homogeneous units against a bid/ask book, rather than exchanging set-collection cards from a replenishing market.

games.controls: Choose side, quantity and price, Post order, Cancel selected order or Advance clearing pulse.
games.finite: Three six-pulse markets with public incoming taker orders and a final delivery obligation.

endless.design: Seeded fresh taker flow, competing quotes and changing delivery requirements; bounded book and pulse count.

games.failure: Miss delivery stock or cash target; cash and sell inventory are reserved by live orders and may not be double-spent.
games.levelsGeneration: Every taker resolves against sorted price/time order; unfilled orders persist and final holdings settle at explicit price.

games.name: Many Hands
games.definingDecision: Contribute part of a personal budget to a threshold public project, pledge conditional matching to change other contributors' incentives, or reserve funds; project benefits are shared even by noncontributors.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Actors spend their own scarce funds on a threshold contribution game with conditional matching and refund rules; there are no council seat weights, policies or bought approval.

games.controls: Choose cash contribution and a matching pledge, then Resolve simultaneous funding.
games.finite: Three multi-project rounds with different threshold/refund/matching rules and rival contribution memories.

endless.design: Seeded project thresholds and benefit distributions with fresh strategic contributors; personal solvency constrains survival.

games.failure: Essential project remains unfunded or final private reserve falls below floor; over-contribution can fail despite public success.
games.levelsGeneration: Public benefit tables, rival conditional rules and matching caps stay visible; generate genuinely feasible thresholds.

games.name: Congestion Crossing
games.definingDecision: Split a fleet among routes whose traversal costs depend on the combined simultaneous load of your fleet and a self-routing rival; an individually shorter road may make every user's journey longer.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Players select simultaneous splittable route flow under load-dependent costs; there is no line topology design, train simulation, queue capacity or passenger transfer.
No temporal phase scheduling: route choices create endogenous travel times even when every route remains open.

games.controls: Allocate fleet units among named paths, inspect cost formulas, then Dispatch both fleets.
games.finite: Three five-day networks, including a visibly tempting cross-link that can induce a worse equilibrium.

endless.design: Seeded affine road costs, fleet budgets and rival adaptation; network size and total fleet remain bounded.

games.failure: Exceed cumulative journey-cost budget; competitive benchmark requires responding to rival load rather than fixed shortest paths.
games.levelsGeneration: Public edge formulas and route-edge incidence tables, with independent brute-force feasible allocations.

games.name: Price of Plenty
games.definingDecision: Choose production quantity before a rival chooses its own; the combined output sets a downward-sloping market price, so individually expanding can destroy joint profit. Capacity investment competes with present production.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Market price is endogenous to rival output and there is no customer-order calendar, shipping pipeline, shelf stock or lost-demand simulation.
A single competitive quantity market with a responsive rival replaces a multi-node material-flow production network.

games.controls: Choose quantity, optionally reserve capital for a capacity upgrade, then Open simultaneous market.
games.finite: Three six-round markets with changing public demand/cost schedules and different rival reactions.

endless.design: Seeded inverse-demand schedules and rival adaptation classes, bounded production capacity and study length.

games.failure: Bankruptcy or missing the final profit quota; output incurs cost even when low market price makes the batch unprofitable.
games.levelsGeneration: Exact integer output/price arithmetic, capped capacity and independently optimized benchmarks.

games.name: Bargain at Closing
games.definingDecision: Offer an allocation of a common pie, accept the rival's counteroffer or reject to retain bargaining rights while the pie shrinks; each party values immediate and delayed shares differently.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Two-party alternating offers, shrinking surplus and credible counteroffers replace multi-faction policy concessions and majority voting.
No spatial parcel cutting or chooser priority: the same divisible surplus is renegotiated under time discount and bilateral rejection.

games.controls: Adjust proposed share, Make offer; on rival offer Accept or Reject.
games.finite: Three sets of three negotiations with public discount factors and differing outside options.

endless.design: Seeded pies, outside options and rival acceptance parameters, bounded rounds; cumulative benefit until quota failure.

games.failure: Closing without agreement or accepting a total payoff below the study quota; rejection visibly shrinks tomorrow's pie.
games.levelsGeneration: Deterministic reservation policy with public bounds, honest rival counteroffers, exact termination at deadline.

games.name: Last Applicant
games.definingDecision: Inspect applicants in irreversible order and stop once to hire; previous candidates cannot be recalled, while inspection cost and a public quality distribution determine the value of waiting.

nearestExisting.differentiator: One irreversible stopping choice ends the search; every candidate leaves forever, and there is no repeated productive arm exploitation or recovery.
No multidimensional packing or accumulating accepted set: select exactly one candidate and surrender all later opportunities.

games.controls: Interview next applicant, Hire current applicant, or decline current applicant permanently.
games.finite: Three hiring campaigns with two or three vacancies and different inspection fees and distributions.

endless.design: New independently seeded applicants drawn without replacement from a visible quality urn, increasing fee capped.

games.failure: Run out of applicants or fail total hired-quality minus interview-fee quota; never silently select the best abandoned applicant.
games.levelsGeneration: Seeded permutation of public quality urn, qualification minima and bounded candidate count; both wins/losses reproducible.

games.name: Seasonal Ledger
games.definingDecision: Assign crops to fields across seasons: legumes restore nitrogen, cereals consume it, consecutive species build pests, and a neighboring companion crop changes yield. Future soil and pest states depend on each field's actual rotation history.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No identical saplings ripening after actions: discrete crop species have persistent field-specific nutrient/pest effects and spatial companionship, with seasons harvested simultaneously.
Agronomic rotation history and yield constraints replace population migration, tax income and urban zoning externalities.
Crops are management choices, not genetic homologs, mating or crossover.

games.controls: Choose a field and its crop, then End season; table previews nitrogen, pests and expected yield.
games.finite: Three four-season farms with distinct soils, market quotas and companion constraints.

endless.design: Seeded soil maps, crop price calendars and quotas; bounded3x2 field and four-season study, difficulty capped.

games.failure: Miss harvest quota or deplete a protected field; repeated high-price cereal is not a dominant strategy because soil/pests persist.
games.levelsGeneration: Public exact agronomic equations, seeded soil heterogeneity and independently searched viable rotations.

games.name: Permit and Progress
games.definingDecision: Bank scarce emission permits across compliance periods, sell surplus into a competitive price schedule or spend capital to retrofit production; selling a permit today can force expensive future abatement when allowance supply tightens.

nearestExisting.differentiator: Compliance tokens are conserved and transferable across periods, while irreversible retrofits change per-unit emissions; no unit startup, ramp, battery or energy balancing.
Goods are legal rights consumed by production obligations and carried across tightening caps; player can alter future consumption through retrofits.

games.controls: Set output, buy/sell a permit, retrofit a plant, then Close compliance period.
games.finite: Three five-period production charters with mandatory delivery, tightening public caps and nontrivial permit opportunity cost.

endless.design: Seeded cap, demand and permit-price calendars with bounded two-plant emission classes; finite charters continue until breach.

games.failure: Uncovered emissions or missed mandatory deliveries loses immediately; permits are consumed once and cannot fund two periods.
games.levelsGeneration: Seeded calendars retain a feasible retrofit/banking route; certify token conservation and correct retrofit timing.

games.name: School of Shoals
games.definingDecision: Choose extraction and an enforceable shared quota for renewable fisheries while autonomous rivals react to their own last catch and your enforcement; taking more now can lower spawning and ruin everyone's later catch.

nearestExisting.differentiator: A common-pool rivalry with strategic extraction, costly enforceable quotas and stock-dependent recruitment replaces centralized predator/prey relocations and fixed intervention choices.
No physical cast timing: fish stock is a shared dynamic resource allocated among competing harvesters.

games.controls: Allocate fleet effort to two grounds, optionally patrol quota, then Harvest season.
games.finite: Three six-season cooperative charters with different growth thresholds and rival effort policies.

endless.design: Seeded growth curves, initial stock and competitor reactions; bounded stock and six-season charters until collapse or quota failure.

games.failure: A breeding ground collapses or community delivery/private cash quota is missed; patrolling reduces harvest capacity and costs real budget.
games.levelsGeneration: Recruitment uses surviving breeding stock, not original stock; all player/rival catches and enforcement are visible.

games.name: Promised Tomorrow
games.definingDecision: Choose cooperation or defection in repeated bilateral exchanges, offer a costly apology to repair trust, and decide whether to switch partners; rivals maintain different observable retaliation and forgiveness memories.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No role claim, hidden card evidence or challenge mechanic: published exchange payoffs and opponent memory make current temptation alter future cooperation.
Pairwise repeated trust games replace multi-party vote thresholds and permanent policy concessions.

games.controls: Select partner, Cooperate or Defect, optionally buy apology before the next exchange.
games.finite: Three eight-exchange communities with public payoff matrices and rival memory classes.

endless.design: Seeded partner memory classes/payoffs and bounded exchange horizon; fresh communities add score until a cooperation/benefit quota fails.

games.failure: Final benefit or reciprocal-cooperation target is missed; constant defection yields short-term gains but burns responsive partners.
games.levelsGeneration: Rival state transitions are explicit and deterministic, with tests for retaliation, forgiveness and apology costs.

games.name: Maturity Garden
games.definingDecision: Build a ladder of zero-coupon claims whose maturity dates match mandatory cash outflows; selling early exposes duration-sensitive prices, while buying a higher long-term return can leave an earlier liability unfunded.

nearestExisting.differentiator: No underwriting premiums, weather losses or reserved collateral: fixed maturity cashflows, dated liabilities and early-sale discount prices determine liquidity.
Assets expire into deterministic dated payouts and prices follow remaining duration, rather than an identical commodity price calendar.

games.controls: Buy or sell one dated claim, inspect the maturity/liability table, then Advance settlement date.
games.finite: Three six-date ledgers with different yield curves, liabilities and reinvestment opportunities.

endless.design: Seeded liability timing and positive bounded yield curves, generated feasible ladders; six-date studies until a settlement default.

games.failure: Insufficient cash at a required settlement loses even if marked asset value is high; matured claims pay exactly once.
games.levelsGeneration: Integer toy claims, explicit discounted sale table, no real investment recommendation; test cash conservation, maturity removal and timing of settlements.
